data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The book has 300 pages, derived by partitioning the 792 digits into three blocks: 9 one-digit page numbers (pages 1\u20139) using 9 digits, 90 two-digit page numbers (pages 10\u201399) using 180 digits, and the remaining 603 digits assigned to three-digit page numbers, which exactly accommodates 201 pages (pages 100\u2013300).","counterconditions":[{"case":"If front matter (e.g., roman numerals) consumed part of the 792-digit budget, then fewer digits remain for arabic-numbered pages and the page count falls below 300.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'pages' means physical leaves rather than numbered sides, the count of leaves would be 150, not 300.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If facing-page spreads are counted once per spread instead of once per page, the allocation of digits to physical sheets changes and the arithmetic no longer holds.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the page numbering skips any numbers (e.g., blank unnumbered pages or plates counted separately), the linear digit-length sum is disrupted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Total digits D(n) = sum_{k=1}^{n} len(k). Split into blocks by digit length: 9\u00d71 = 9 digits for 1\u20139, 90\u00d72 = 180 digits for 10\u201399. Remainder after the two-digit block: 792 \u2212 9 \u2212 180 = 603. Since each subsequent page number uses 3 digits, the count of three-digit pages is 603 / 3 = 201. Adding to the base of 99 gives 99 + 201 = 300 pages. The remainder after division by 3 is exactly zero, so the digit budget is exactly exhausted with no partial page.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
